world 2 (key portable).reader_note: "printed his on linen in sixteen panels hinged to fold flat" gives portable away.

world 3 (key rigorous).reader_note: 'walked every main road with a measuring chain and fixed each town by sightings of the stars' gives rigorous; prescient is a weak second.

world 0 (key prescient).reader_note: "the canal dug in 1840 follows his line, and the three villages became the kingdom's chief mill towns" gives prescient.

world 2 (key ornament).reader_note: Repainting and feast-day lamps plus locked doors with no use; "doors stayed locked" kills refuge and platform, repainting kills quarry.

world 3 (key quarry).reader_note: The 1860 survey sentence (emblem stones in sixty houses' foundations and the bridge) alone gives quarry.

world 0 (key refuge).reader_note: "families from the lower streets who lodged in it for weeks at a time" during wet springs gives refuge outright.

world 1 (key platform).reader_note: 'the candidates took turns on that balcony on successive market mornings' makes platform both literal and figurative.

world 3 (key porous).reader_note: Group-by-group exemptions give porous, but obsolete fits "fewer than one household in five"; only "still owed the duty" and "partly cleared" keep the rule alive.

world 0 (key obsolete).reader_note: Easy: 'the old ditches were filled in and built over' makes obsolete immediate, and 'last called the spring muster in 1858' kills onerous.

world 2 (key profitable).reader_note: Fines exceed the crews' cost ('a fraction of what it collected') gives profitable; 'less than half of what a laborer earned' kills onerous; porous is a near-miss.

world 1 (key proxy).reader_note: "multiplying the valley's figures by each district's area" makes it a stand-in; prototype is the near miss.

world 3 (key reservoir).reader_note: Crews drawn whenever a district fell behind gives reservoir of labor; outpost literally fits a remote eastern district.

world 0 (key prototype).reader_note: 'printed the valley's revised plan as its standard drawing, from which the terraces of nine other districts were then built' is the definition of prototype.

world 3 (key rampart).reader_note: Weekly attacks on each merger plan, each withdrawn, city kept its council: rampart; rudder (steering civic opinion) is a near miss.

world 1 (key rudder).reader_note: Six hundred measures passing or failing as advised gives rudder; ritual literally fits a weekly fifty-year column.

world 1 (key professionalized).reader_note: 'certificate... two years of full-time training... monthly wage' gives professionalized in one sentence; petrified is the only near-miss.

world 3 (key repurposed).reader_note: Fish carriers turned into furnishings gives repurposed; 'weaving more baskets than ever' makes rekindled a near-miss, though the craft never lapsed.

world 2 (key overshadowed).reader_note: Overshadowed needs the molten-rock papers plus the never-run dye tests; orphaned is strongly defensible since the hypothesis was left untested and unclaimed.

world 3 (key orphaned).reader_note: Survey confirmed the ridge source but removed the volcano theory that explained it, leaving textbooks without a why; pruned is a close second.

world 0 (key rehabilitated).reader_note: 'set the idea aside' plus 'again presented the ridge as the springs' source' gives rehabilitated; 'The 1931 survey' is introduced with a definite article as if already known.

world 1 (key pivot).reader_note: Pivot follows from chapter eleven of twenty-two plus fortunes rising before and falling after; pawn is a weak second.

world 2 (key pawn).reader_note: "He does whatever the last sister to speak with him asks" points to pawn; pivot is defensible since his errands move the quarrel.

world 3 (key puzzle).reader_note: Unexplained acts plus 'offers no motive for any of these acts' give puzzle; pivot is defensible since the locket thread runs through him.
